title: CREST CCT — Network Services
description: Covers the Network Services (PT005) domain of the CREST Certified Tester (CCT) examination. Topics include enumeration and exploitation of common network services (FTP, SSH, SMTP, DNS, SMB, LDAP, SNMP, RDP, MSSQL, etc.), service fingerprinting, credential attacks, and privilege escalation via network services.

questions.question: During a penetration test, you connect to an FTP server and successfully log in with the username 'anonymous' and an email address as the password. What is this type of access called?
questions.explanation: Anonymous FTP allows users to connect without a real account by using 'anonymous' as the username and typically any email address as the password, often exposing sensitive files to unauthenticated users.

questions.question: Which FTP mode requires the client to open a listening port for the server to connect back to for data transfer?
questions.explanation: In active mode FTP, the client sends a PORT command specifying a port it is listening on, and the server initiates the data connection back to the client — which often fails through firewalls and NAT.

questions.question: Why is FTP considered insecure for transmitting credentials over a network?

options.A: It uses weak symmetric encryption for passwords
options.B: It transmits credentials in cleartext, making them visible to packet sniffers
options.C: It stores passwords in reversible Base64 encoding on the server

questions.explanation: FTP sends usernames and passwords in plaintext over the network, allowing any attacker with packet capture capability on the network path to intercept credentials directly.

questions.question: Which tool is commonly used to brute-force FTP credentials during a penetration test?
questions.explanation: Hydra (THC-Hydra) is a fast and flexible network login cracker that supports numerous protocols including FTP, SSH, HTTP, and many others for credential brute-forcing.

questions.question: An SSH server is configured to accept only key-based authentication. Which file on the server specifies the public keys authorised to log in as a given user?
questions.explanation: The ~/.ssh/authorized_keys file contains the public keys that are permitted to authenticate as that user; each line represents one authorised key.

questions.question: Which OpenSSH vulnerability allowed remote attackers to enumerate valid usernames by measuring response time differences?
questions.explanation: CVE-2018-15473 allowed attackers to determine whether a username existed on an OpenSSH server by sending malformed authentication requests and observing different server responses for valid versus invalid usernames.

questions.question: Which SSH feature allows a penetration tester to forward traffic from a local port through an encrypted SSH tunnel to reach a service on an internal network?
questions.explanation: SSH local port forwarding (ssh -L) binds a local port and tunnels traffic through the SSH connection to a specified destination host and port, enabling access to internal services through a compromised SSH server.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the SSH known_hosts file on a client system?

options.A: It stores the client's private keys for authentication
options.B: It records the public host keys of previously connected servers to detect MITM attacks
options.C: It contains a list of users permitted to use SSH
options.D: It defines the cipher suites the client will accept

questions.explanation: The known_hosts file stores server host key fingerprints; if a server's key changes unexpectedly, SSH warns the user of a potential man-in-the-middle attack.

questions.question: A penetration tester discovers a Telnet service running on an embedded device. What is the primary security concern with this protocol?

options.A: Telnet uses weak DES encryption that can be cracked in real time
options.B: Telnet transmits all data including credentials in cleartext
options.D: Telnet is vulnerable to SYN flood attacks by design

questions.explanation: Telnet sends all communication, including usernames and passwords, as unencrypted plaintext, making it trivial for an attacker to capture credentials via network sniffing.

questions.question: Which protocol was designed as the secure replacement for Telnet?
questions.explanation: SSH (Secure Shell) was developed as a cryptographically secure replacement for Telnet, providing encrypted remote shell access and authentication.

questions.question: During SMTP enumeration, which command can a penetration tester use to verify whether a specific email address exists on the mail server?
questions.explanation: The SMTP VRFY command asks the server to verify whether a given email address or username exists, enabling user enumeration when the server responds differently for valid and invalid addresses.

questions.question: What is an SMTP open relay, and why is it a security concern?

options.A: A server that encrypts all outgoing email — it may leak encryption keys
options.B: A server that allows unauthenticated users to send email to any external domain — it can be abused for spam and phishing
options.C: A server that stores emails in plaintext — credentials may be exposed
options.D: A server that forwards all email to a backup MX — it creates a single point of failure

questions.explanation: An open relay accepts and forwards email from any sender to any recipient without authentication, making it exploitable for sending spam, phishing emails, or conducting social engineering attacks.

questions.question: Which SMTP command can be used to enumerate mailing list members on a misconfigured mail server?
questions.explanation: The EXPN command expands a mailing list or alias, revealing all member email addresses — a valuable source of valid usernames during enumeration.

questions.question: A tester uses the SMTP RCPT TO command with various email addresses and notes that the server returns '250 OK' for valid addresses and '550 User unknown' for invalid ones. What attack is being performed?

options.C: SMTP user enumeration via RCPT TO

questions.explanation: Differential responses to RCPT TO commands reveal which email addresses are valid on the server, allowing enumeration of user accounts even when VRFY and EXPN are disabled.

questions.question: What is SMTP header injection?

options.A: Injecting SQL queries into the SMTP authentication mechanism
options.B: Injecting additional email headers (such as BCC or Subject) via user-controlled input in a web application's email function
options.C: Replacing the SMTP banner to disguise the mail server software
options.D: Intercepting SMTP traffic with a proxy to modify headers in transit

questions.explanation: SMTP header injection occurs when user input is incorporated into email headers without sanitisation, allowing attackers to inject additional headers like BCC to send copies of emails to themselves.

questions.question: Which command-line tool and syntax would a penetration tester use to attempt a DNS zone transfer against the domain example.com from nameserver ns1.example.com?
questions.explanation: The 'dig axfr' command requests a full zone transfer (AXFR) from the specified nameserver, which if permitted will return all DNS records for the domain.

questions.question: Which DNS record type maps a hostname to an IPv6 address?
questions.explanation: AAAA (quad-A) records map a hostname to a 128-bit IPv6 address, analogous to how A records map hostnames to IPv4 addresses.

questions.question: Which DNS record type specifies the mail servers responsible for receiving email for a domain?
questions.explanation: MX (Mail Exchange) records specify the mail servers and their priorities for a domain, directing email delivery to the correct servers.

questions.question: A penetration tester discovers that a DNS server allows zone transfers to any requesting host. What information can be obtained?

options.A: Only the SOA record for the domain
options.B: A complete listing of all DNS records in the zone, revealing hostnames, IP addresses, and network topology
options.C: The DNSSEC signing keys for the zone
options.D: The DNS server's configuration file and credentials

questions.explanation: An unrestricted zone transfer returns every DNS record in the zone, exposing internal hostnames, IP addresses, mail servers, and other infrastructure details useful for mapping the target network.

questions.question: Which DNS record type is used for reverse DNS lookups, mapping an IP address to a hostname?
questions.explanation: PTR (Pointer) records provide reverse DNS resolution, mapping an IP address back to its associated hostname within the in-addr.arpa (IPv4) or ip6.arpa (IPv6) zone.

questions.question: During HTTP reconnaissance, which HTTP method can be used to determine which methods a web server supports?
questions.explanation: The OPTIONS method returns the HTTP methods supported by the server for a given resource, often revealing potentially dangerous methods like PUT, DELETE, or TRACE.

questions.question: A penetration tester sends the request 'GET /../../etc/passwd HTTP/1.1' to a web server. What attack is being attempted?
questions.explanation: Directory traversal (path traversal) uses sequences like ../ to escape the web root directory and access arbitrary files on the server's filesystem.

questions.question: Which tool can be used to grab the HTTP banner of a web server and identify its software version?

options.B: Nmap with the -sV flag or curl -I

questions.explanation: Nmap's service version detection (-sV) probes open ports to identify server software and versions, while 'curl -I' retrieves HTTP response headers that often include the Server banner.

questions.question: What is the primary security advantage of POP3S (port 995) over POP3 (port 110)?

options.A: POP3S uses stronger password hashing algorithms
options.B: POP3S encrypts the entire communication channel using TLS, preventing credential interception
options.D: POP3S stores emails in an encrypted format on the server

questions.explanation: POP3S wraps the POP3 protocol in TLS encryption, protecting credentials and email content from being captured by network sniffers, unlike plaintext POP3 on port 110.

questions.question: Which protocol retrieves email from a server and, by default on port 143, transmits credentials in cleartext?
questions.explanation: IMAP on port 143 transmits login credentials in plaintext by default; IMAPS on port 993 should be used instead to encrypt the connection with TLS.

questions.question: In a Kerberos environment, what condition must an account meet to be vulnerable to AS-REP Roasting?

options.A: The account must have a Service Principal Name (SPN) set
options.B: The account must have the 'Do not require Kerberos preauthentication' flag enabled
options.C: The account must be a member of the Domain Admins group
options.D: The account must have an expired password

questions.explanation: AS-REP Roasting targets accounts that have Kerberos pre-authentication disabled, allowing an attacker to request an AS-REP containing data encrypted with the user's password hash for offline cracking.

questions.question: What is a Golden Ticket attack in a Kerberos environment?

options.A: Cracking a TGS ticket obtained via Kerberoasting
options.B: Forging a Ticket Granting Ticket (TGT) using the KRBTGT account's NTLM hash, granting domain-wide access
options.C: Replaying a captured TGT from a domain administrator
options.D: Exploiting a vulnerability in the KDC to bypass authentication entirely

questions.explanation: A Golden Ticket is a forged TGT created using the KRBTGT account's NTLM hash, allowing the attacker to impersonate any user and access any resource in the domain for the ticket's lifetime.

questions.question: How does a Silver Ticket attack differ from a Golden Ticket attack?

options.A: A Silver Ticket forges a TGS ticket using a service account's NTLM hash, granting access to a specific service rather than the entire domain
options.B: A Silver Ticket targets Linux-based Kerberos implementations only
options.C: A Silver Ticket requires compromising the KRBTGT account
options.D: A Silver Ticket exploits weak cipher suites in the KDC

questions.explanation: A Silver Ticket forges a Ticket Granting Service (TGS) ticket using the NTLM hash of a specific service account, providing access only to that service without contacting the KDC.

questions.question: Which tool is commonly used to perform Kerberoasting by requesting TGS tickets for accounts with SPNs in an Active Directory environment?
questions.explanation: Rubeus (Windows) and Impacket's GetUserSPNs.py (Linux) are the standard tools for Kerberoasting — they request TGS tickets for all accounts with SPNs and output them in a format suitable for offline cracking.

questions.question: In a Pass-the-Ticket attack, what does the attacker use to authenticate to network services?

options.B: A captured or forged Kerberos ticket (TGT or TGS)

questions.explanation: Pass-the-Ticket involves stealing or forging Kerberos tickets from memory (using tools like Mimikatz) and injecting them into the current session to authenticate as the ticket owner.

questions.question: What does an LDAP null bind allow an attacker to do?

options.A: Authenticate as the LDAP administrator with a blank password
options.B: Connect to the LDAP server without providing any credentials and potentially query directory information
options.C: Inject LDAP queries to bypass web application authentication
options.D: Encrypt LDAP traffic using a self-signed certificate

questions.explanation: An LDAP null bind (anonymous bind) allows connecting to the directory without credentials; if the server permits unauthenticated queries, an attacker can enumerate users, groups, and other directory objects.

questions.question: Which port does LDAP typically operate on?
questions.explanation: LDAP operates on TCP port 389 by default; LDAPS (LDAP over TLS) uses port 636 for encrypted connections.

questions.question: During a penetration test, you successfully establish an SMB null session to a Windows host. What can you typically enumerate?

options.A: The contents of all shared folders
options.B: Share names, user accounts, group memberships, and password policies
options.C: The SAM database with all password hashes

questions.explanation: SMB null sessions allow unauthenticated enumeration of shares, users, groups, and domain policies, providing valuable reconnaissance information without valid credentials.

questions.question: What is the significance of SMB signing in a Windows Active Directory environment?

options.A: SMB signing encrypts all file transfers between client and server
options.B: SMB signing prevents NTLM relay attacks by ensuring message integrity and authenticity
options.C: SMB signing restricts SMB access to domain-joined machines only
options.D: SMB signing replaces Kerberos authentication for SMB connections

questions.explanation: SMB signing adds a cryptographic signature to each SMB message, preventing attackers from tampering with or relaying captured NTLM authentication messages in relay attacks.

questions.question: Which vulnerability, tracked as MS17-010, allows remote code execution via SMBv1 and was infamously exploited by the WannaCry ransomware?
questions.explanation: EternalBlue (MS17-010) is a critical vulnerability in Microsoft's SMBv1 implementation that allows remote code execution; it was weaponised by the WannaCry and NotPetya campaigns.

questions.question: In an NTLM relay attack, what is the role of a tool like Responder?

options.A: It cracks NTLM hashes using rainbow tables
options.B: It poisons LLMNR/NBT-NS/mDNS responses to capture NTLM authentication attempts from victims on the network
options.C: It performs Kerberoasting against Active Directory
options.D: It patches the EternalBlue vulnerability on SMB servers

questions.explanation: Responder poisons name resolution protocols (LLMNR, NBT-NS, mDNS) to trick victims into authenticating to the attacker's machine, capturing NTLMv1/v2 hashes or relaying them with ntlmrelayx.

questions.question: Which tool is used in conjunction with Responder to relay captured NTLM authentication to other services on the network?
questions.explanation: ntlmrelayx from the Impacket suite relays captured NTLM authentications to target services (SMB, LDAP, HTTP, MSSQL), potentially gaining code execution or modifying Active Directory objects.

questions.question: Which tool is commonly used to enumerate SMB shares, users, and groups from a Linux attacking machine?
questions.explanation: enum4linux is a wrapper around smbclient, rpcclient, and net commands designed to enumerate information from Windows/Samba hosts via SMB, including shares, users, groups, and password policies.

questions.question: What are the default SNMP community strings commonly found on misconfigured devices?
questions.explanation: SNMP v1/v2c devices are frequently left with the default community strings 'public' for read-only access and 'private' for read-write access, allowing unauthenticated information disclosure or configuration changes.

questions.question: Which command-line tool walks the SNMP MIB tree to enumerate all available information from an SNMP-enabled device?
questions.explanation: snmpwalk queries the entire MIB tree (or a subtree) of an SNMP agent, retrieving all available OIDs which can reveal system information, network interfaces, routing tables, running processes, and installed software.

questions.question: How does SNMPv3 improve security over SNMPv1 and v2c?

options.A: SNMPv3 uses TLS encryption for all communication
options.B: SNMPv3 adds username-based authentication, message integrity, and optional encryption instead of relying on cleartext community strings
options.C: SNMPv3 removes the ability to write configuration changes
options.D: SNMPv3 restricts access to the loopback interface only

questions.explanation: SNMPv3 introduces the User-based Security Model (USM) with authentication (MD5/SHA) and privacy (DES/AES) capabilities, replacing the insecure community string model of v1/v2c.

questions.question: Which critical vulnerability in Microsoft's Remote Desktop Protocol implementation allowed pre-authentication remote code execution and was dubbed 'BlueKeep'?
questions.explanation: BlueKeep (CVE-2019-0708) is a critical use-after-free vulnerability in RDP that allows unauthenticated remote code execution on Windows systems without Network Level Authentication enabled.

questions.question: What is Network Level Authentication (NLA) in the context of RDP, and why is it important?

options.A: NLA encrypts the RDP session with AES-256
options.B: NLA requires the user to authenticate before a full RDP session is established, reducing the attack surface for pre-authentication vulnerabilities
options.C: NLA restricts RDP access to local network connections only
options.D: NLA enforces multi-factor authentication for all RDP connections

questions.explanation: NLA requires authentication via CredSSP before the RDP session is fully established, meaning exploits targeting the RDP protocol itself (like BlueKeep) cannot be reached without valid credentials.

questions.question: A penetration tester gains access to a MSSQL server as the 'sa' account. Which stored procedure can be enabled to execute operating system commands?
questions.explanation: xp_cmdshell is a MSSQL extended stored procedure that allows execution of arbitrary operating system commands; it is disabled by default but can be re-enabled by the sa account via sp_configure.

questions.question: In MSSQL, how can an attacker use UNC path injection to capture NTLM hashes?

options.A: By modifying the SQL Server's registry keys to redirect authentication
options.B: By using xp_dirtree or xp_fileexist with a UNC path pointing to an attacker-controlled SMB server, forcing the SQL service to authenticate
options.C: By injecting a UNC path into the SQL Server connection string
options.D: By exploiting the MSSQL Browser service to redirect connections

questions.explanation: Functions like xp_dirtree('\\attacker-ip\share') cause the SQL Server to initiate an SMB connection to the attacker's server, sending the SQL service account's NTLM hash which can be captured by Responder.

questions.question: What is a linked server in MSSQL, and how can it be exploited?

options.A: A linked server is a backup MSSQL instance that mirrors all data
options.B: A linked server is a connection to another database server that can be queried remotely, and may run with higher privileges allowing privilege escalation
options.C: A linked server is a failover cluster node
options.D: A linked server is a read-only replica used for reporting

questions.explanation: Linked servers allow MSSQL to query other database servers via OPENQUERY; if the linked server connection uses a higher-privileged account (e.g., sa), an attacker can escalate privileges by executing commands through the link chain.

questions.question: On a MySQL server, what security risk does allowing remote root login present?

options.A: The root account cannot use prepared statements remotely
options.B: It enables brute-force attacks against the highest-privileged database account from any network location
options.C: Remote root connections bypass all SQL query logging
options.D: Remote root access disables MySQL's built-in encryption

questions.explanation: Allowing remote root login exposes the most privileged MySQL account to network-based brute-force and credential-stuffing attacks from anywhere that can reach the database port.

questions.question: How can MySQL User Defined Functions (UDFs) be used for privilege escalation on a Linux host?

options.A: UDFs automatically elevate MySQL to run as root
options.B: A shared library can be loaded as a UDF to execute operating system commands with the privileges of the MySQL service account
options.C: UDFs bypass MySQL's authentication mechanism entirely

questions.explanation: By writing a malicious shared object to the MySQL plugin directory and creating a UDF from it, an attacker can execute OS commands as the MySQL service user, potentially escalating to root if MySQL runs with elevated privileges.

questions.question: Which command is used to discover NFS exports available on a remote server?
questions.explanation: The 'showmount -e' command queries the NFS server's export list, revealing which directories are shared and which hosts are permitted to mount them.

questions.question: In VoIP/SIP security testing, what is the purpose of the tool svmap?

options.A: It captures and decodes VoIP call audio
options.B: It scans a network to identify SIP devices and their capabilities
options.C: It performs denial-of-service attacks against SIP proxies
options.D: It encrypts SIP traffic using SRTP

questions.explanation: svmap is part of the SIPVicious toolkit and scans a network range to identify SIP-enabled devices such as phones, PBXes, and gateways by sending SIP requests and analysing responses.

questions.question: What is the primary security risk associated with TFTP (port 69)?

options.A: TFTP uses weak MD5 checksums for file integrity
options.B: TFTP provides no authentication mechanism, allowing anyone to read or write files
options.C: TFTP encrypts files with a default shared key
options.D: TFTP only supports plaintext file formats

questions.explanation: TFTP has no authentication or access control mechanism whatsoever; any client that can reach the TFTP server can read or write files, making it a target for extracting router configurations and other sensitive data.

questions.question: A penetration tester discovers TFTP running on a network device. What is a common file they might try to retrieve?

options.B: The device's running configuration file (e.g., running-config on Cisco devices)

questions.explanation: Network device configurations often contain credentials, SNMP community strings, and network topology information; TFTP is frequently used by routers and switches for configuration backup and can be exploited to retrieve these files.

questions.question: On a Linux system, which file contains the password hashes and is readable only by root?
questions.explanation: /etc/shadow stores the actual password hashes and is restricted to root access (typically mode 640 or 600), while /etc/passwd is world-readable but no longer contains password hashes.

questions.question: What information about user accounts is stored in /etc/passwd on a Linux system?

options.A: Username, encrypted password hash, UID, GID, home directory, and shell
options.B: Username, UID, GID, GECOS field, home directory, and login shell (with 'x' as password placeholder)
options.D: Username, SSH public key, and last login timestamp

questions.explanation: /etc/passwd contains colon-delimited fields including username, password placeholder ('x' indicating the hash is in /etc/shadow), UID, GID, GECOS comment, home directory, and login shell.

questions.question: Which password cracking tool supports GPU acceleration and is commonly used to crack password hashes offline?
questions.explanation: Hashcat is specifically designed for GPU-accelerated offline password hash cracking, supporting hundreds of hash types and multiple attack modes including dictionary, brute-force, and rule-based attacks.

questions.question: In Hashcat, what does the attack mode '-a 0' specify?
questions.explanation: Hashcat's -a 0 is the straight (dictionary) attack mode, which tests each word from a wordlist against the target hashes, optionally combined with rules to mutate the candidates.

questions.question: In Hashcat, what does the attack mode '-a 3' specify?
questions.explanation: Hashcat's -a 3 is the brute-force (mask) attack mode, where the attacker defines character sets and positions using mask syntax (e.g., ?u?l?l?l?d?d) to generate all possible candidates matching the pattern.

questions.question: What does Hashcat attack mode '-a 6' do?

options.B: It performs a hybrid attack appending mask characters to each dictionary word
options.D: It reverses each word in a dictionary before testing

questions.explanation: Hashcat's -a 6 is a hybrid dictionary + mask attack that appends mask-generated characters to each word from a dictionary (e.g., wordlist + ?d?d appends all two-digit combinations to each word).

questions.question: What is a rainbow table, and why has it become less effective against modern password storage?

options.A: A database of encrypted passwords — modern encryption is unbreakable
options.B: A precomputed table mapping hashes to plaintext passwords — salted hashes render rainbow tables ineffective since each password produces a unique hash
options.C: A colour-coded chart of password complexity — modern passwords exceed the chart's range
options.D: A network map of password servers — modern systems use decentralised authentication

questions.explanation: Rainbow tables are precomputed hash-to-plaintext lookup tables; salting passwords with a unique random value before hashing means each user's hash is different even for identical passwords, defeating precomputed tables.

questions.question: Which network redundancy protocol operates at Layer 3 and can be hijacked by an attacker sending higher-priority advertisements to become the active router?
questions.explanation: HSRP uses priority values to elect the active router; an attacker can send forged HSRP advertisements with a higher priority to take over as the active router, enabling traffic interception.

questions.question: How can an attacker exploit Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) to perform a man-in-the-middle attack?

options.A: By flooding the switch's MAC table to force it into hub mode
options.B: By sending superior BPDUs to become the root bridge, causing all traffic to flow through the attacker's switch
options.C: By exploiting ARP cache poisoning via STP frames
options.D: By disabling all switch ports through STP topology changes

questions.explanation: An attacker sends Bridge Protocol Data Units (BPDUs) with a lower bridge priority to become elected as the root bridge, forcing network traffic to be rerouted through their device for interception.

questions.question: Which protocol, similar to HSRP but vendor-neutral and defined in RFC 5798, allows virtual router redundancy and can be similarly hijacked?
questions.explanation: VRRP (Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol) is the standards-based equivalent of Cisco's HSRP; it can be hijacked by advertising higher-priority VRRP packets to take over the virtual router role.

questions.question: Which Nmap scan type sends a SYN packet to each target port and determines its state based on the response, without completing the TCP three-way handshake?
questions.explanation: A SYN scan (half-open scan) sends a SYN packet and classifies the port based on the response: SYN-ACK means open, RST means closed; the handshake is never completed, making it faster and less likely to be logged.

questions.question: A penetration tester uses SSH dynamic port forwarding (ssh -D) to create a SOCKS proxy. What does this allow?

options.A: Forwarding a single specific port to a remote host
options.B: Routing arbitrary traffic from any application through the SSH tunnel as a SOCKS proxy
options.C: Establishing a VPN connection through the SSH server
options.D: Decrypting SSH traffic from other users on the same server

questions.explanation: SSH -D creates a local SOCKS proxy that tunnels all proxied application traffic through the SSH connection, enabling the tester to access multiple internal services without setting up individual port forwards.

questions.question: What is the default port for Kerberos authentication?
questions.explanation: Kerberos uses TCP/UDP port 88 for communication between clients and the Key Distribution Center (KDC), which handles authentication requests and ticket granting.

questions.question: Which DNS record type contains human-readable text data and is often used for SPF, DKIM, and domain verification records?
questions.explanation: TXT records hold arbitrary text data and are commonly used for email authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), domain ownership verification, and other metadata purposes.

questions.question: Which DNS record type indicates the authoritative nameserver for a domain and contains zone administration information such as serial number and refresh intervals?
questions.explanation: The SOA (Start of Authority) record contains zone metadata including the primary nameserver, responsible person's email, zone serial number, and timing parameters for zone transfers and caching.

questions.question: A penetration tester discovers an SNMP service with the community string 'private'. What level of access does this typically grant?

options.B: Read-write access, potentially allowing configuration changes on the device
options.C: Administrative access to the management console
options.D: Access to encrypted SNMP v3 credentials

questions.explanation: The default 'private' community string typically grants read-write access to the SNMP agent, potentially allowing an attacker to modify device configurations, change settings, or even execute commands.

questions.question: Which tool can a penetration tester use to perform credential spraying against RDP services?
questions.explanation: Crowbar is a brute-forcing tool that supports RDP, SSH, VNC, and OpenVPN; it is particularly effective for RDP credential spraying as it supports NLA authentication.

questions.question: What file permissions should /etc/shadow have on a properly configured Linux system?
questions.explanation: /etc/shadow should be readable only by root (and optionally the shadow group), with permissions of 640 or 600; any broader permissions would allow non-privileged users to read password hashes.

questions.question: In a rule-based password cracking attack, what does a 'rule' do?

options.A: It defines the hash algorithm to use for cracking
options.B: It applies transformations to dictionary words (such as appending numbers, capitalising, or substituting characters) to generate additional candidates
options.C: It sets the GPU temperature limit during cracking
options.D: It specifies which network ports to target for online brute-forcing

questions.explanation: Rules define character manipulations applied to each word in a dictionary — such as toggling case, appending digits, or performing leet-speak substitutions — significantly expanding the candidate space without a larger wordlist.

questions.question: Which SSH cipher is considered weak and should be disabled on modern SSH servers?
questions.explanation: The arcfour (RC4) cipher has known cryptographic weaknesses including biases in its keystream and should be disabled in favour of modern ciphers like AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305.

questions.question: A penetration tester wants to use SSH remote port forwarding (ssh -R) to expose an internal web service to their attack machine. What does this achieve?

options.A: It forwards a port on the SSH server back to the client's local network, making a client-side service accessible from the server side
options.B: It encrypts HTTP traffic between the browser and the web server
options.C: It creates a reverse shell connection to the attacker
options.D: It disables SSH host key verification for the connection

questions.explanation: SSH -R binds a port on the remote (server) side and forwards connections through the SSH tunnel to a host and port accessible from the client, effectively exposing a local or internal service to the remote network.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the DNS NS record type?

options.A: It maps a hostname to an IP address
options.B: It delegates authority for a domain or subdomain to a specific nameserver
options.C: It creates an alias for another hostname
options.D: It specifies the mail server for a domain

questions.explanation: NS (Name Server) records delegate a DNS zone to authoritative nameservers, indicating which servers are responsible for answering queries about that domain.

questions.question: What type of DNS record creates an alias, pointing one hostname to another?
questions.explanation: A CNAME (Canonical Name) record creates an alias that points one domain name to another, allowing multiple names to resolve to the same host without duplicating A records.

questions.question: During a penetration test of VoIP infrastructure, what risk does unencrypted SIP signalling present?

options.A: SIP messages will be rejected by firewalls
options.B: Attackers can eavesdrop on call setup details, capture credentials, and potentially intercept or redirect calls
options.C: The PBX will automatically disable itself
options.D: Only the caller ID will be exposed

questions.explanation: Unencrypted SIP transmits call setup information, authentication credentials, and call routing data in cleartext, allowing attackers to intercept calls, capture credentials, and perform call redirection attacks.

questions.question: On a compromised MSSQL server, which command would an attacker use to enable xp_cmdshell if it is disabled?

options.A: EXEC sp_configure 'show advanced options', 1; RECONFIGURE; EXEC sp_configure 'xp_cmdshell', 1; RECONFIGURE;
options.B: ALTER DATABASE master SET xp_cmdshell = ON
options.C: GRANT EXECUTE ON xp_cmdshell TO public
options.D: CREATE PROCEDURE xp_cmdshell AS EXEC cmd.exe

questions.explanation: Enabling xp_cmdshell requires first enabling advanced options via sp_configure, then enabling xp_cmdshell itself, with RECONFIGURE after each change to apply the settings.

questions.question: Which Nmap script can be used to check if an SMB server is vulnerable to the EternalBlue (MS17-010) exploit?
questions.explanation: The Nmap script smb-vuln-ms17-010 specifically tests for the EternalBlue vulnerability by sending crafted SMB packets and analysing the server's response to determine if it is unpatched.

questions.question: What is the difference between LDAP (port 389) and LDAPS (port 636)?

options.A: LDAP supports only read operations while LDAPS supports read and write
options.B: LDAPS encrypts the LDAP connection using TLS/SSL, while standard LDAP communicates in cleartext
options.C: LDAPS requires Kerberos authentication while LDAP supports simple bind
options.D: LDAP and LDAPS are different protocols with incompatible schemas

questions.explanation: LDAPS wraps the standard LDAP protocol in a TLS/SSL encrypted connection on port 636, preventing credential interception and data eavesdropping that is possible with cleartext LDAP on port 389.

questions.question: An attacker exploits an NFS share with no_root_squash enabled by creating a SUID binary on the mounted share. What is the impact?

options.A: The binary will run with the NFS server's service account privileges
options.B: The SUID binary will execute as root on the NFS server when run by any local user, enabling privilege escalation
options.C: The binary will be automatically removed by NFS security mechanisms
options.D: The SUID bit is stripped when files are created over NFS

questions.explanation: With no_root_squash, a remote root user can create a root-owned SUID binary on the NFS share; any user on the NFS server who executes this binary will gain root privileges through the SUID mechanism.

questions.question: Which of the following tools is specifically designed for subdomain enumeration through DNS?
questions.explanation: Sublist3r is a subdomain enumeration tool that combines search engine scraping, DNS brute-forcing, and third-party data sources to discover subdomains associated with a target domain.

questions.question: In an NTLM relay attack, why is it important that SMB signing is not enforced on the target?

options.A: SMB signing slows down the connection, making relay attacks impractical
options.B: SMB signing requires the attacker to know the session key to sign messages, which is not available in a relay scenario, causing authentication to fail
options.C: SMB signing encrypts the NTLM hash, preventing its capture
options.D: SMB signing requires mutual certificate authentication

questions.explanation: When SMB signing is enforced, each message must be signed with a key derived from the user's password; the relaying attacker doesn't possess this key and cannot generate valid signatures, causing the relayed session to be rejected.

questions.question: Which Kerberos component issues Ticket Granting Tickets (TGTs) and Ticket Granting Service (TGS) tickets?
questions.explanation: The KDC (Key Distribution Center), which runs on Domain Controllers, contains the Authentication Service (AS) that issues TGTs and the Ticket Granting Service (TGS) that issues service tickets.

questions.question: Which FTP mode is generally preferred when clients are behind NAT or firewalls, and why?

options.A: Active mode, because the server initiates connections which bypass client-side firewalls
options.B: Passive mode, because the client initiates both control and data connections, avoiding the need for inbound connections to the client
options.C: Extended mode, because it tunnels data through the control connection
options.D: Implicit mode, because it uses TLS for all connections

questions.explanation: Passive mode has the server listen on a random high port and the client initiates the data connection, avoiding issues with client-side firewalls and NAT that would block the server's inbound connection in active mode.

questions.question: During a penetration test, you discover a web server that responds to the HTTP TRACE method. What attack does this potentially enable?

options.B: Cross-Site Tracing (XST), which can steal HttpOnly cookies by reflecting them in the TRACE response
options.C: Remote code execution via TRACE buffer overflow
options.D: Directory traversal via TRACE request paths

questions.explanation: Cross-Site Tracing (XST) exploits the TRACE method which echoes the entire request back to the client, including cookies marked as HttpOnly, potentially allowing an attacker to steal them via client-side scripting.

questions.question: What is credential spraying, and why is it effective against services like RDP?

options.A: Trying many passwords against a single account to find the correct one
options.B: Trying a small number of commonly used passwords against many accounts simultaneously, avoiding account lockout thresholds
options.C: Spraying captured hashes across multiple services for pass-the-hash
options.D: Using rainbow tables against all accounts in a domain

questions.explanation: Credential spraying tries a few common passwords (like 'Summer2024!') against many accounts, staying under lockout thresholds; it is effective against RDP because many organisations have users with weak passwords.

questions.question: Which John the Ripper utility is used to combine the /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow files into a single file suitable for cracking?
questions.explanation: The 'unshadow' utility merges /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow into a single file in the format John the Ripper expects, combining user information with the corresponding password hashes.

questions.question: An attacker captures an NTLMv2 hash using Responder. Which tool and approach would they use to crack it?

options.A: John the Ripper with the --format=NT flag
options.B: Hashcat with mode 5600 (NetNTLMv2) and a wordlist
options.C: Ophcrack with Windows XP rainbow tables
options.D: Mimikatz to decrypt the hash directly

questions.explanation: Hashcat mode 5600 is specifically designed for cracking NetNTLMv2 hashes (captured from network authentication); combined with a good wordlist and rules, it efficiently recovers the plaintext password.

questions.question: What SNMP OID subtree is commonly walked to enumerate running processes on a Linux system?
questions.explanation: The hrSWRunTable OID (1.3.6.1.2.1.25.4.2) contains information about running processes including process names, paths, and parameters, revealing installed software and services on the target system.

questions.question: Which SIPVicious tool is used to enumerate valid SIP extensions (user accounts) on a PBX?
questions.explanation: svwar (SIP War dialer) enumerates valid SIP extensions/accounts on a PBX by sending REGISTER or INVITE requests and analysing the responses to distinguish between valid and invalid extensions.

questions.question: What is the primary risk of using SNMPv1 on network devices?

options.A: SNMPv1 does not support GET requests
options.B: SNMPv1 transmits community strings in cleartext, providing no authentication security
options.D: SNMPv1 is limited to IPv6 networks only

questions.explanation: SNMPv1 sends community strings as plaintext over the network, meaning anyone capturing network traffic can obtain the community string and gain read or read-write access to the SNMP agent.

questions.question: In a penetration test, you gain access to a MySQL server as root and want to read the file /etc/passwd from the underlying operating system. Which SQL statement would you use?
questions.explanation: MySQL's LOAD_FILE() function reads a file from the server's filesystem and returns its contents as a string, provided the MySQL user has the FILE privilege and the file is readable by the MySQL process.

questions.question: What countermeasure prevents HSRP hijacking on a network?

options.B: Configuring HSRP authentication with a strong key and using MD5 authentication
options.C: Enabling port security on all switch ports
options.D: Disabling ARP on the router interfaces

questions.explanation: HSRP MD5 authentication ensures that only routers with the correct authentication key can participate in HSRP, preventing attackers from injecting forged HSRP advertisements with higher priority.

questions.question: Which switch security feature prevents STP manipulation attacks by restricting which ports can receive BPDUs?
questions.explanation: BPDU Guard disables a port if it receives a BPDU (Bridge Protocol Data Unit), preventing rogue devices from participating in STP elections and attempting to become the root bridge.

questions.question: Which Nmap flag enables OS detection, version scanning, script scanning, and traceroute in a single command?
questions.explanation: Nmap's -A flag enables aggressive scanning which combines OS detection (-O), version detection (-sV), script scanning (-sC), and traceroute (--traceroute) in one comprehensive scan.

questions.question: When performing a dictionary attack with John the Ripper, which flag specifies the wordlist file to use?
questions.explanation: The --wordlist flag followed by the path to a wordlist file tells John the Ripper to perform a dictionary attack using the specified wordlist instead of its default incremental (brute-force) mode.

questions.question: A penetration tester discovers LDAP on a target and successfully performs an anonymous query that returns user objects with their descriptions. Some descriptions contain passwords. What vulnerability has been found?

options.A: LDAP injection in a web application
options.B: Sensitive information disclosure through LDAP anonymous bind combined with poor data hygiene

questions.explanation: Allowing anonymous LDAP queries combined with storing sensitive information (like passwords) in user-readable attributes such as the description field is a common Active Directory misconfiguration that leads to credential exposure.

questions.question: In an HTTP response, which header reveals the web server software and version, useful for banner grabbing?
questions.explanation: The 'Server' response header typically reveals the web server software name and version (e.g., Apache/2.4.41 or nginx/1.18.0), providing valuable information for identifying known vulnerabilities.

questions.question: Which tool from the Impacket suite can be used to perform AS-REP Roasting against Active Directory accounts without pre-authentication?
questions.explanation: GetNPUsers.py from Impacket requests AS-REP data for accounts without Kerberos pre-authentication required, producing hashes that can be cracked offline to recover account passwords.

questions.question: What is the MSSQL SA (System Administrator) account, and why is it a high-value target?

options.A: A read-only service account used for database monitoring
options.B: The default highest-privileged database account with full control over the MSSQL instance, often able to execute OS commands
options.C: A Windows domain account used for SQL Server replication
options.D: A backup account that can only restore databases

questions.explanation: The SA account is the built-in MSSQL sysadmin account with unrestricted access to the database engine; compromising it allows enabling xp_cmdshell, accessing all databases, and often achieving OS-level command execution.

questions.question: What is the security risk of VoIP call eavesdropping, and how is it typically performed?

options.A: An attacker exploits the PBX to place premium-rate calls at the organisation's expense
options.B: An attacker captures RTP (Real-time Transport Protocol) packets containing the audio stream and reconstructs them to listen to conversations
options.C: An attacker sends malformed SIP INVITE packets to crash the PBX
options.D: An attacker uses DNS rebinding to redirect SIP traffic

questions.explanation: VoIP call audio is transmitted via RTP, often unencrypted; an attacker on the same network can capture RTP packets using tools like Wireshark and reconstruct the audio stream to eavesdrop on conversations.

questions.question: Which SIPVicious tool is used to brute-force SIP extension passwords?
questions.explanation: svcrack performs online password cracking against SIP accounts by attempting authentication with different passwords for a given SIP extension, supporting both REGISTER and INVITE methods.

questions.question: Which SMB enumeration technique allows listing available shares on a remote Windows host using a null session?
questions.explanation: 'net view' on Windows or 'smbclient -L -N' (null session) on Linux lists available SMB shares on a remote host, revealing file shares, printers, and IPC$ shares that may contain sensitive data.

questions.question: What is the significance of the IPC$ share in SMB null session enumeration?

options.A: IPC$ stores the server's Internet connection settings
options.B: IPC$ (Inter-Process Communication) is used for named pipes and allows RPC calls, enabling user and group enumeration via null sessions
options.C: IPC$ contains backup copies of all shared files
options.D: IPC$ is the hidden administrative share for the C: drive

questions.explanation: The IPC$ share facilitates inter-process communication via named pipes; null session access to IPC$ enables attackers to make RPC calls for enumerating users, groups, shares, and domain policies.

questions.question: A penetration tester discovers that a DNS server responds to queries for internal domain names from external sources. What is this called?

options.B: DNS information leakage through a split-horizon misconfiguration

questions.explanation: When a DNS server configured for split-horizon DNS incorrectly serves internal records to external queries, it leaks internal hostnames and IP addresses that should only be visible within the organisation.

questions.question: In the context of SSH key-based authentication, what is the risk of a private key file with permissions 644?

options.A: The SSH server will encrypt it with a weaker algorithm
options.B: Other users on the system can read the private key, potentially impersonating the key owner
options.C: The key will expire more quickly due to excessive reads
options.D: SSH will automatically generate a new key pair

questions.explanation: A private key with 644 permissions is readable by all users on the system; SSH clients typically refuse to use keys with overly permissive permissions, but if used, any local user could copy and use the key.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the NFS 'root_squash' option, and what happens when it is enabled?

options.A: It compresses all files owned by root to save disk space
options.B: It maps remote root user (UID 0) to the anonymous/nobody user, preventing remote root from having root privileges on the NFS server
options.C: It prevents the root user from mounting NFS shares
options.D: It encrypts all files owned by root on the NFS share

questions.explanation: root_squash is the default NFS security mechanism that maps the remote root user to nobody/nfsnobody, ensuring that a client's root user cannot read or write files as root on the server's filesystem.

questions.question: Which Hashcat flag specifies the hash type being cracked?
questions.explanation: The -m flag in Hashcat specifies the hash mode (e.g., -m 0 for MD5, -m 1000 for NTLM, -m 5600 for NetNTLMv2), telling Hashcat which algorithm to use when attempting to crack the provided hashes.

questions.question: An attacker on a local network runs Responder and captures NTLMv2 hashes. The hashes resist cracking with a wordlist. What alternative attack can the attacker perform with these hashes?

options.A: Pass-the-hash directly to authenticate to SMB
options.B: Relay the authentication in real-time to another target using ntlmrelayx (NTLM relay attack)
options.C: Downgrade the hashes to LM format for easier cracking
options.D: Convert the NTLMv2 hashes to Kerberos tickets

questions.explanation: Net-NTLMv2 hashes cannot be used for pass-the-hash (only NTLM hashes can), but the authentication can be relayed in real-time to other services using ntlmrelayx, gaining access without cracking the password.

questions.question: Which Linux password hashing algorithm is indicated by the $6$ prefix in /etc/shadow?
questions.explanation: The $6$ prefix in /etc/shadow indicates SHA-512 based hashing (sha512crypt); other prefixes include $1$ for MD5, $2a$/$2b$ for bcrypt, and $5$ for SHA-256.

questions.question: Which technique does an attacker use when they request Kerberos AS-REP responses for a list of usernames without needing valid credentials?
questions.explanation: AS-REP Roasting allows an attacker to request encrypted AS-REP data for any account with pre-authentication disabled, using only a list of usernames — no existing credentials are needed to initiate the request.

questions.question: Which MSSQL system stored procedure can be used to list the contents of a directory on the underlying operating system?
questions.explanation: xp_dirtree lists the directory structure of a specified path on the OS filesystem; it requires fewer permissions than xp_cmdshell and can also be abused for UNC path injection to capture NTLM hashes.

questions.question: What protocol does SNMP use for transport, and on which ports does it operate?
questions.explanation: SNMP primarily uses UDP with port 161 for agent queries (GET/SET operations) and port 162 for receiving traps (unsolicited notifications from agents to the management station).

questions.question: What is the security concern with the HTTP PUT method being enabled on a web server?

options.A: PUT allows clients to upload or overwrite files on the server, potentially enabling web shell deployment
options.B: PUT reveals the server's internal directory structure
options.C: PUT allows cross-site scripting via uploaded headers

questions.explanation: The HTTP PUT method allows clients to upload files directly to the web server; if enabled without proper authentication, an attacker can upload malicious files such as web shells to gain remote code execution.

questions.question: During an engagement, you identify a MySQL server running on port 3306 that accepts remote connections. Which Nmap script would you use to enumerate databases?
questions.explanation: The Nmap mysql-databases script connects to a MySQL server (with provided credentials) and lists all available databases, helping identify targets for further exploitation.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of using SFTP or SCP over traditional FTP for file transfer?

options.A: SFTP and SCP are faster than FTP due to compression
options.B: SFTP and SCP encrypt all data and credentials in transit using SSH, while FTP transmits everything in cleartext
options.C: SFTP and SCP support larger file sizes than FTP
options.D: SFTP and SCP do not require authentication

questions.explanation: SFTP (SSH File Transfer Protocol) and SCP (Secure Copy Protocol) operate over an encrypted SSH channel, protecting both credentials and file data from interception, unlike FTP which sends everything in plaintext.

questions.question: Which Impacket tool can be used to remotely execute commands on a Windows system via SMB using a semi-interactive shell?
questions.explanation: Impacket's psexec.py uploads a service binary to the target via SMB, creates and starts a Windows service, and provides a semi-interactive command shell, similar to the Sysinternals PsExec tool.

questions.question: Which LDAP attribute in Active Directory stores the plaintext or reversible-encrypted password and is a common target during LDAP enumeration?
questions.explanation: The ms-MCS-AdmPwd attribute stores the local administrator password set by LAPS (Local Administrator Password Solution); if LDAP permissions are misconfigured, non-privileged users may be able to read this attribute.

questions.question: Why should Telnet services be specifically checked during a penetration test of IoT and embedded devices?

options.A: IoT devices use a proprietary encrypted version of Telnet
options.B: Many IoT and embedded devices still ship with Telnet enabled using default or hardcoded credentials, providing easy initial access
options.C: Telnet on IoT devices is immune to brute-force attacks
options.D: IoT Telnet services always run on non-standard ports

questions.explanation: Despite being obsolete on servers, Telnet remains common on IoT devices, routers, and embedded systems, often with default or hardcoded credentials that provide immediate administrative access.

questions.question: Which SMTP command is used to initiate a mail transaction by specifying the sender's email address?
questions.explanation: MAIL FROM specifies the sender's address (envelope sender) and begins a new mail transaction; this command is followed by one or more RCPT TO commands to specify recipients.
